claims.text: The system is a single-crystal FeNiCrCoCu coating on a single-crystal Cu matrix.
At 300 K, the initial coating has a high density of stacking faults and dislocations.
The simulated nanoindentation depth is 30 Å and the indenter velocity is 10 m/s.
Above 900 K, rapid thermal activation triggers stacking-fault annihilation.
Above 900 K, stacking faults are annihilated faster than dislocation nucleation can replenish mobile dislocations.
The imbalance between stacking-fault annihilation and dislocation nucleation produces dislocation starvation.
Dislocation starvation prevents strain hardening and prevents the coating from sustaining plastic flow by slip.
The loss of slip-mediated plasticity concentrates stress at the contact interface and triggers localized amorphization.
Transient amorphous zones arise through stacking-fault collapse and exhaustion of mobile dislocations.
The interfacial amorphous phase has lower shear strength and higher adhesion.
Localized amorphization causes the friction-coefficient spike and catastrophic loss of wear resistance.
The friction coefficient increases sharply between 900 K and 1000 K as amorphization begins.
After the spike, the friction coefficient plateaus or decreases because the thickening amorphous layer acts as a solid lubricant.
Wear resistance above 900 K drops precipitously relative to its value at 600 K.
At 600 K, dislocation density is reduced but remains sufficient to preserve elastic modulus and hardness without amorphization.
In polycrystalline material, grain boundaries may supply dislocations and mitigate dislocation starvation.
Artificially seeding a high density of HCP stacking faults and dislocations will prevent or reduce dislocation starvation at 1000 K.
If starvation-driven amorphization is responsible, the seeded simulation will exhibit a smaller friction spike and a lower amorphous fraction than the unseeded simulation.
Persistence of the friction spike under high dislocation density and low amorphization would favor lattice thermal softening over the proposed starvation/amorphization mechanism.

contradictions.description: The intervention correctly describes 10 m/s as an indenter velocity, whereas the conditions field labels 10 m/s as a strain rate. Strain rate has units of inverse time, so these are not equivalent quantities.
